alignments.note: Inferential conjunction rendered *Wherefore*.
Imperative verb.

Negator with a **plain** indefinite: `τι` carries no negation of its own, so under rule 59 the single English word answers to both tokens and they form one `aligned` unit, *no-* spelling the negator and *-thing* the indefinite. Rule 41 does not apply, the second word not being a negative.
Preposition rendered *before*.
Anarthrous noun with a supplied determiner, a rule 51 helper on the noun since no article competes.

`ἕως ἄν` rendered by a single English word: rule 50 makes this one `aligned` unit headed on that word, as MAT.10.11 and MAT.10.23 read `ἕως ἂν` → *till*. Leaving `ἄν` `unrepresented` is the failure rule 50 names.
Article rendered *the* (rule 19).
Noun.
Aorist subjunctive rendered by the bare English *come*.
Relative pronoun.
Future verb with its auxiliary; *bring to light* is a support frame whose complement carries the sense of `φωτίζω`, so rule 17 heads on *light*. Discontinuous around *both* under rule 15.
Correlative particle rendered *both*.
Article governing a substantival adjective takes both the determiner and the supplied generic noun under rule 102, headed on the supplied noun; the adjective stays bare.
Substantival adjective left its own bare word under rule 102.
The ASV writes no determiner for *darkness*, so the article has nothing to anchor and is `unrepresented` under rule 23; the case preposition stays with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause.
Genitive rendered *of darkness*, headed on the noun (rule 17).
Conjunction.
*make manifest* is a support frame; rule 17 heads on the meaning-bearing complement, as *make straight* heads on *straight*. The single *will* has already been spent on s014.
Article rendered *the*.
Noun.
Article carrying its case preposition; *of the* is one unit headed on *the* (rules 17 and 21).
Noun standing bare after the article took the determiner.
Conjunction.
Adverb.
The ASV recasts `γενήσεται` as *shall … have*; the auxiliary rides with the verb and the head is the lexical *have* (rules 9 and 17). Discontinuous under rule 15.
Distributive rendered *each man*; *man* is the supplied generic completion, so rule 17 keeps the head on the quantifying word, as rule 69 heads *any man* on *any*.

The ASV supplies a possessive for this article. `ἑκάστῳ` is the only candidate possessor and has already been spent on *each man*, so under rule 76's availability test it cannot take the determiner and the article does, as rule 20's second arm requires.
Noun standing bare after the article took the possessive.
Preposition rendered *from*.
Article before a name with no English realization (rule 23).
Name.

review_notes: All 33 source and 39 target ids are partitioned exactly once.
`ἕως ἄν` is joined into one unit on *until* under rule 50's count-of-English-words test; splitting and leaving `ἄν` empty is the failure that rule names.
`μὴ … τι` → *nothing* is joined under rule 59; a reference comparison expecting the negator alone will report this as a disagreement.
